com.esignal.jstandard.managers

Interface MarketDepthManager

  • All Superinterfaces:
    ResourceManager

    public interface MarketDepthManager
extends ResourceManager
    Purpose of this class is to provide resources of MarketDepth records.

    MarketDepthManager allows users to subscribe and unsubscribe to the eSignal symbols. The users are required to pass in a listener for each symbol they subscribe to and the type of MarketDepth view that they are interested in.

    All the MarketDepth updates are sent to the listener for that symbol. In this way, multiple listeners can be attached for the same symbol and/or MarketDepth type by calling subscribe method multiple times with different MarketDepthListener. After a successful subscribe the listeners will start listening to the streaming Market Maker information depending on the view that was selected. The updated MarketDepth information wrapped as a List can be retrieved using the MarketDepthEvent fired with new data. We will run through a simple usage of MarketDepthManager.

    Let's create a factory first. The getFactory() method will retrieves the default implementation of the Factory. The implementation can be changed by calling other getFactory(...) methods OR overriding property "jstandard.resourcemanagerfactory.name" in jstandard.properties. ResourceManagerFactory factory = ResourceManagerFactory.getFactory();

    Now create a MarketDepthManager using the factory. MarketDepthManager marketDepthManager = factory.createMarketDepthManager();

    To start the connection we now need to create instances of ConnectionSettings and ConnectionListener. (Implement MyConnectionListener) ConnectionSettings myConnectionSettings = new ConnectionSettings("myhost", "myusername", "mypassword"); //If proxy settings are required //myConnectionSettings.setProxyInfo("phost", pport, "puser", "ppass"); ConnectionListener myConnectionListener = new MyConnectionListener(); //Set the new connection flag for the new market depth API myConnectionSettings.setFlags(CONNECTION_FLAGS.DBCAPI_FLAG_DEPTH_EX.getCode()); marketDepthManager.connect(myConnectionSettings, myConnectionListener); At the start the connection listener will receive an event of connecting and after successful connection connected event.

    To start receiving updates for the symbol, let's subscribe to the MarketDepthManager with "GOOG" symbol. But before that we also need to have an implementation of the MarketDepthListener. Let's say we have two listeners: LoggerMarketDepthListener and MyMarketDepthListener. MarketDepthListener loggerMarketDepthListener = new LoggerMarketDepthListener(); MarketDepthListener myMarketDepthListener = new MyMarketDepthListener(); Fill the Market Depth Request Now : int depthType = eDEPTH_TYPE.ORDER_BOOK.getCode(); int depthSource = eDEPTH_SOURCE.NASDAQ.getCode(); int depthFilter = eDEPTH_FILTER.DEFAULT.getCode(); boolean useDefault = true; String symbol = "GOOG"; Long turnAround = generateUniqueTurnAround(); MarketDepthRequest req = new DefaultMarketDepthRequest(symbol, turnAround, depthSource, depthType, depthFilter, useDefault); marketDepthManager.subscribe(symbol, loggerMarketDepthListener, req); marketDepthManager.subscribe(symbol, myMarketDepthListener, req); Now both the listeners will start receiving the updates on the same symbol GOOG at that depthTYpe, source and filter.

    To receive the updated data please implement MarketDepthListeners' onUpdate method. From MarketDepthEvent get the MarketDepthList object which should have updated information. The MarketDepthList object is a list of MarketDepth objects that could have one or more updated fields. 

     
        public void onUpdate(MarketDepthEvent event) {
                System.out.println("symbol update was received for market depth.");
                List<MarketDepth> marketDepthList = event.getMarketDepthList();
                for(MarketDepth depth : marketDepthList)
                {
                        if(depth instanceof OrderBookRecord)
                        {
                                OrderBookRecord aDepth = (OrderBookRecord)depth;
                                aDepth.getOrderId();
                        }
                }
                System.out.println("Update List:\n" + marketDepthList);
        }

    Let's say we decide to unsubscribe from the LoggerMarketDepthListener for the symbol GOOG. Use the same instance that was created while subscribing. marketDepthManager.unsubscribe(symbol, loggerMarketDepthListener, turnAround); Now only myMarketDepthListener will receive updates for the symbol GOOG.

    Disconnect from the manager in the end. marketDepthManager.disconnect(); Since we did not unsubscribe for myMarketDepthListener, calling disconnect will make sure appropriate calls are made before closing the connection.

    Since:
    01-001-0008
    Author:
    Interactive Data Corporation
    See Also:
    MarketDepthListener, MarketDepthRequest, NetOrderImbalanceRequest

      • subscribe

        void subscribe(java.lang.String symbol,
               MarketDepthListener marketDepthListener,
               MarketDepthRequest marketDepthRequest)
        This method subscribes the given symbol and sends updates to the given MarketDepthListener. The MarketDepthRequest can be used to feed in different values and set them for the depthType, depthSource and depthFilter. This is done to make the API flexible new sources and types for future use. The User can take the use of the MarketDepthRequest.eDEPTH_TYPE , MarketDepthRequest.eDEPTH_SOURCE and MarketDepthRequest.eDEPTH_FILTER enums and get the codes to feed them into the MarketDepthRequest.
        Parameters:
        symbol - Valid Symbol value
        marketDepthListener - MarketDepthListener value
        marketDepthRequest - MarketDepthRequest object with the request params populated.
        Since:
        01-08-000
